title: Multilinearity of top intersection numbers
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be a nonempty proper $k$-scheme of dimension $g\geq1$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let $\mathcal L_1,\ldots,\mathcal L_g$ be invertible modules [def-sc-invertible-module]. The intersection number $(\mathcal L_1\cdots\mathcal L_g\cdot X)$ [def-sc-intersection-number] is invariant under isomorphism, symmetric in its entries and additive under tensor product in each entry. Thus replacing the $i$th entry by $\mathcal M\otimes\mathcal N$ gives the sum of the two intersection numbers with $\mathcal M$ and with $\mathcal N$ in that entry. The value with a trivial entry is zero, and replacing an entry by its dual negates the value. These operations extend uniquely by rational multilinearity to rational linear combinations of isomorphism classes of invertible modules, with the relations $[\mathcal M\otimes\mathcal N]=[\mathcal M]+[\mathcal N]$.

source.place: Tag 0BER, lemma-intersection-number-additive; Definition 0BEP, definition-intersection-number (symmetry); rational extension of the additive pairing

proof.text: Use [def-sc-intersection-number] with the identity closed immersion $X\to X$. By [lem-sc-snapper-numerical-polynomial], its Euler-characteristic function, and the function for any finite list of invertible modules, is represented by a rational polynomial of total degree at most $g$. Here the coherent module is $\mathcal O_X$, whose support is all of $X$; the identity case and its degree bound are explicitly included in [def-sc-intersection-number]. We may identify such polynomials from their values on integer tuples. Indeed, induct on the number of variables: for fixed integer values of all but the first variable, [lem-trf-polynomial-infinite-evaluation-identity] over $\mathbf Q$ identifies the two polynomials in the first variable, since they agree on all integers. Each coefficient of their difference, a polynomial in the remaining variables, therefore vanishes on all remaining integer tuples and is zero by induction. The zero-variable case is equality of constants.

source.place: Tags 0BEP and 0BEL; uniqueness of the representing rational polynomial

proof.text: An isomorphism of any entry induces an isomorphism of each tensor twist, and hence of its cohomology groups; their dimensions and the alternating sum defining $\chi$ in [def-pc-euler-characteristic] agree. Permuting the entries permutes the exponents of the same tensor product, by the symmetry isomorphism of tensor products of modules. Thus the representing polynomial is unchanged under entry isomorphisms and has its variables permuted under entry permutations, by step 1. The coefficient of $n_1\cdots n_g$ is unchanged by these permutations. By [def-sc-intersection-number] this proves isomorphism invariance and symmetry.

source.place: Definition 0BEP, symmetry of its coefficient construction

proof.text: Fix the other $g-1$ entries, with variables $t_1,\ldots,t_{g-1}$, and replace the remaining entry by $\mathcal M\otimes\mathcal N$. Apply [lem-sc-snapper-numerical-polynomial] to the list consisting of those entries, $\mathcal M$, and $\mathcal N$, obtaining $Q(t_1,\ldots,t_{g-1},u,v)$ of total degree at most $g$. Its substitutions $Q(t,z,z)$, $Q(t,z,0)$, and $Q(t,0,z)$ are the polynomials for $\mathcal M\otimes\mathcal N$, $\mathcal M$, and $\mathcal N$, respectively: at every integer tuple this follows from $(\mathcal M\otimes\mathcal N)^{\otimes z}\cong\mathcal M^{\otimes z}\otimes\mathcal N^{\otimes z}$, also for negative $z$ by duals, and step 1 identifies the polynomials. A monomial contributing to the coefficient of $t_1\cdots t_{g-1}z$ in $Q(t,z,z)$ must have each $t$ exponent one and $u,v$ exponents adding to one. Thus only $t_1\cdots t_{g-1}u$ and $t_1\cdots t_{g-1}v$ contribute, each with multiplicity one. Their coefficients are exactly those extracted from $Q(t,z,0)$ and $Q(t,0,z)$. By [def-sc-intersection-number] this is the required additivity. Symmetry allows any slot.

source.place: Tag 0BER, lemma-intersection-number-additive, proof expanded by coefficient extraction

proof.text: Write $I(\mathcal L)$ for the value in a fixed slot. As $\mathcal O_X\otimes\mathcal O_X\cong\mathcal O_X$, additivity gives $I(\mathcal O_X)=2I(\mathcal O_X)$, hence $I(\mathcal O_X)=0$. For an invertible module, evaluation $\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal L^\vee\to\mathcal O_X$ is an isomorphism: on every rank-one trivializing open of [def-sc-invertible-module] it is multiplication $\mathcal O_X\otimes\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_X$, and these evaluation maps agree on overlaps. Consequently $0=I(\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal L^\vee)=I(\mathcal L)+I(\mathcal L^\vee)$, giving the dual clause.

source.place: Consequence of Tag 0BER and the rank-one module definition

proof.text: Let $V$ be the rational vector space of finite rational linear combinations of isomorphism classes of invertible modules, modulo the relations $[\mathcal M\otimes\mathcal N]-[\mathcal M]-[\mathcal N]$. For $v_i=\sum_j a_{ij}[\mathcal L_{ij}]$ define the extended value to be $\sum_{j_1,\ldots,j_g}(\prod_{i=1}^g a_{i j_i}) (\mathcal L_{1j_1}\cdots\mathcal L_{gj_g}\cdot X)$. Isomorphism invariance makes each summand independent of representatives. Expanding a generating relation in any slot gives zero by step 3, also when multiplied by any rational scalar, so the formula descends to $V^g$. It is rational multilinear by distributivity of the finite sum and symmetric by step 2. Every rational multilinear extension must have this same finite-sum formula, proving uniqueness. The assumption $g\ge1$ ensures that the trivial-entry and dual assertions refer to an existing slot.

source.place: Rational multilinear extension of Tag 0BER, explicit finite-sum construction

lean.statement: theorem top_intersection_multilinear (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [IsProper (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [Nonempty X] (g : ℕ) (_hg : 1 ≤ g) (hd : topologicalKrullDim X = ((g : ℕ∞) : WithBot ℕ∞)) : (∀ (L M : Fin g → X.Modules) [∀ j, (L j).IsInvertible] [∀ j, (M j).IsInvertible], (∀ j, Nonempty (L j ≅ M j)) → intersectionNumber k X X (𝟙 X) g hd L = intersectionNumber k X X (𝟙 X) g hd M) ∧ (∀ (L M : Fin g → X.Modules) [∀ j, (L j).IsInvertible] [∀ j, (M j).IsInvertible] (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin g)), (∀ j, Nonempty (M j ≅ L (σ j))) → intersectionNumber k X X (𝟙 X) g hd M = intersectionNumber k X X (𝟙 X) g hd L) ∧ (∀ (L M N : Fin g → X.Modules) [∀ j, (L j).IsInvertible] [∀ j, (M j).IsInvertible] [∀ j, (N j).IsInvertible] (i : Fin g), (∀ j, j ≠ i → M j = L j ∧ N j = L j) → Nonempty (L i ≅ M i ⊗ N i) → intersectionNumber k X X (𝟙 X) g hd L = intersectionNumber k X X (𝟙 X) g hd M + intersectionNumber k X X (𝟙 X) g hd N) ∧ (∀ (L : Fin g → X.Modules) [∀ j, (L j).IsInvertible] (i : Fin g), Nonempty (L i ≅ 𝟙_ X.Modules) → intersectionNumber k X X (𝟙 X) g hd L = 0) ∧ (∀ (L M : Fin g → X.Modules) [∀ j, (L j).IsInvertible] [∀ j, (M j).IsInvertible] (i : Fin g), (∀ j, j ≠ i → M j = L j) → Nonempty (M i ≅ (L i).dual) → intersectionNumber k X X (𝟙 X) g hd M = -intersectionNumber k X X (𝟙 X) g hd L) ∧ (∃ F : MultilinearMap ℚ (fun _ : Fin g ↦ ℚ ⊗[ℤ] Additive X.Pic) ℚ, (∀ (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin g)) (v : Fin g → ℚ ⊗[ℤ] Additive X.Pic), F (v ∘ σ) = F v) ∧ (∀ (L : Fin g → X.Modules) [∀ j, (L j).IsInvertible], F (fun j ↦ (1 : ℚ) ⊗ₜ[ℤ] Additive.ofMul (Pic.ofIsInvertible (L j))) = intersectionNumber k X X (𝟙 X) g hd L) ∧ ∀ G : MultilinearMap ℚ (fun _ : Fin g ↦ ℚ ⊗[ℤ] Additive X.Pic) ℚ, (∀ (L : Fin g → X.Modules) [∀ j, (L j).IsInvertible], G (fun j ↦ (1 : ℚ) ⊗ₜ[ℤ] Additive.ofMul (Pic.ofIsInvertible (L j))) = intersectionNumber k X X (𝟙 X) g hd L) → G = F)
